result.summary: The image shows a dark, enclosed underpass with no pedestrian facilities. The environment is highly hostile, lacking sidewalks, crosswalks, or adequate lighting, forcing pedestrians to share the roadway with vehicles.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Facility
hazards.description: There is no sidewalk or designated walking area, forcing pedestrians into the roadway.

hazards.name: Poor Visibility and Lighting
hazards.description: The underpass environment is dark with limited artificial lighting, making pedestrians difficult to see.

interventions.title: Construct Protected Walkway

result.summary: The image depicts a hostile pedestrian environment within a highway underpass or tunnel. There is a complete lack of dedicated pedestrian infrastructure, with only a narrow shoulder separated by a concrete barrier from multiple lanes of high-speed traffic.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Facility
hazards.description: There is no paved walkway for pedestrians, forcing anyone on foot into a narrow, unprotected shoulder area.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the roadway behind the concrete barrier

hazards.name: High-Speed Traffic Environment
hazards.description: The multi-lane tunnel configuration suggests high vehicle speeds with no physical separation for pedestrians other than a low concrete barrier.

hazards.name: Poor Visibility and Lighting
hazards.description: The underpass environment creates significant shadows and glare, making pedestrians difficult for drivers to see.

interventions.title: Protected Pedestrian Walkway
interventions.description: If pedestrian access is necessary, a raised and physically separated walkway with a high-tension guardrail or wall should be installed.

interventions.title: Enhanced Tunnel Lighting
interventions.description: Install high-visibility LED lighting specifically designed for underpasses to eliminate dark spots and improve driver sightlines.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Prohibition Signage
interventions.description: If the facility is not intended for pedestrian use, clear signage should be posted at all entrances to prevent foot traffic from entering a dangerous environment.
interventions.source: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)
